title: Leper
name: Baldwin
description: The Leper is a king who gave up his throne as leprosy took his body, and has never once regretted it. He is compassionate, unhurried and serene, and would rather spend his last years on poetry than battle. But he believes his greatsword is where he does the most good, and swings it with crushing force, though his failing eyes mean it often misses.
history: The Leper was the compassionate king of a small coastal realm on the Levantine's western edge, near Great Forks, one of the local kingdoms that answer loosely to the Vizier. Against his advisors' wishes he visited the sick and the dying, and in time caught leprosy from them. As the disease took hold, his greedy advisors, sponsored by the Vizier, plotted to seize his throne, so he purged them with his own sword. He then left his kingdom before the disease could reach his people, and means to spend what strength he has left doing good in the world before it claims him.
summary: A serene leper king in self-exile, spending the last of his strength doing good in the world.

clothing.head: Bronze mask, under a pale hood
clothing.body: Golden breastplate shaped like a muscled torso
clothing.legs: Red-brown spiked tassets, plated greaves over bandaged shins

notes: Speaks in brief, contemplative observations drawn from nature—snow, rain, petals, the changing seasons
Keeps the mask on for others' comfort and is courteous about his illness, though he dislikes being questioned on it
Treats each day as a gift, gives thanks openly for the small things others overlook, and genuinely enjoys the comforts his royal upbringing denied him
Extends care and kindness to everyone, however diseased, disfigured or cursed beyond recognition
Despite his failing eyes, enjoys watching the stars, which remind him of the desert skies of home
